sourceOfTruth: This manifest is the checked-in source for rendering parity coverage. Reports are generated from it.

entries.title: Four-plane scene tile storage and scene coordinates
entries.nextAction: Keep the region-window contract and add an extended-tile fixture.

entries.title: Complete RuneLite Scene API surface
entries.reason: The tracked RuneLite rendering-relevant Scene API surface now has an explicit neutral disposition and concrete contracts for every semantic shape needed by Map Studio. SceneContract carries base coordinates, map-region identity, minimum level, world-view identity, instance identity, and API classification; roof regions/removal are first-class; InstanceTemplateGrid exposes the exact client-shaped [plane][13][13] packed template view with the current OSRS bit layout and -1 sentinel; and ExtendedSceneLayout models RuneLite's documented 104x104 normal scene inside the 184x184 extended coordinate space at offset 40. Presentation-only and mutation-only APIs remain deliberately outside authored scene state, while the actual extended-border traversal and rotated instance rendering are independently tracked under scene.extendedTiles and scene.instances rather than being hidden inside this umbrella item.
entries.nextAction: Keep SceneContract, InstanceTemplateGrid, ExtendedSceneLayout, and the roof contracts stable as the Scene API boundary. Complete extended-border camera traversal under scene.extendedTiles and rotated instance rendering under scene.instances without reopening the API-surface contract.

entries.title: Extended tile border context
entries.reason: RuneLite's 104x104 normal scene and 184x184 extended top-level scene are represented explicitly, including the 40-tile / five-zone offset and the 13x13 normal zone footprint centered inside the 23x23 root GPU zone grid. ExtendedSceneZoneLayout reproduces the top-level draw-zone translation used by GpuPlugin.drawZoneOpaque/drawZoneAlpha while leaving sub-worldviews unshifted. RSPSi retains geometry by absolute 8x8 WorldZoneCoordinate instead of rebasing arrays; GpuUploadPlan now carries SceneWindow metadata through both full and incremental compilation, and GpuCommandVisibility consumes it every native frame to keep the full five-zone border eligible while rejecting zones outside the 184x184 root domain. Camera movement changes only frame visibility metadata and never the geometry/upload fingerprint. A combined fixture verifies that connected roof removal remains an independent earlier scene projection and does not discard valid extended-border geometry.
entries.nextAction: Keep extended traversal as a frame-time zone gate over absolute resident geometry. Instance-template rotation/projection remains separately tracked under scene.instances; do not duplicate that work in the extended-scene contract.

entries.title: Shared corner heights and tile interpolation
entries.nextAction: Add a native height-gradient acceptance fixture.

entries.title: Tile shape, overlay, underlay, and rotation topology
entries.nextAction: Compare all shape IDs against an external revision-240 fixture.

entries.title: Bridge links, effective plane, and authored height
entries.reason: Bridge projection is now explicit instead of overloaded into one effective-plane integer. Every scene tile carries authored/source plane, current scene plane, original/render level, and minimum/plane-cull level. RuneLite's setLinkBelow behavior is represented by shifting the current scene plane while retaining the original render level; the visibility-below flag can independently force the minimum/cull level to zero. Packet fingerprints and bridge fixtures cover the complete tuple.
entries.nextAction: Keep the explicit plane tuple and bridge fixtures as regression coverage when roof/min-level traversal and instance scenes are added.

entries.title: OSRS terrain lighting and color math
entries.nextAction: Lock byte-exact terrain light outputs in revision-240 fixtures, and compare a textured interior (e.g. Lumbridge castle 3232,3207) against a RuneLite GPU capture.
entries.reason: 2026-09-23: textured floors were recoloured into the tile's hue (the shader rebuilt each texel from the tile HSL plus texel luminance, and TerrainPacketBuilder injected the texture average hue into the vertex colour). The client keeps the texture's own RGB and multiplies it by a bare 7-bit light: textured overlay colour is -1 (runescape-client class470 scene tile builder), the textured span multiplies each texel channel by the shade (class272), and RuneLite gpu/frag.glsl computes texture * (hsl / 127) with a < 1 discarded. Both are now matched.

entries.title: Roof removal, minimum level, and camera visibility
entries.reason: RuneLite roof removal is modeled as derived scene semantics plus transient frame state. RoofRegionMap reproduces buildRoofs() from tile flag 0x4 with plane/y/x region numbering, eight-neighbour blocking connectivity, and the one-tile non-blocking perimeter. RoofRemovalState reproduces POSITION, HOVERED, DESTINATION, and the camera-to-player BETWEEN mode, including the exact if/else walk, blocking-only region selection, camera-pitch < 310 gate, final-player-tile exclusion, and coordinate-bounds behavior across sparse scene tiles. CLIENT_TRAVERSAL now preserves vanilla physical-level culling when the mode is disabled and, when enabled, replaces it with the selected connected-region test used by RSSceneMixin. Scene minimum-level traversal and the editor-wide static roof-geometry toggle remain separate concerns.
entries.nextAction: Keep RoofRegionMap and RoofRemovalState as the shared roof contract. Instance-template coordinate projection remains tracked separately under scene.instances, and extended-border traversal remains tracked under scene.extendedTiles.

entries.title: Instance template chunks and rotated regions
entries.reason: Packed [plane][13][13] instance templates now reconstruct a derived 104x104 scene before ordinary terrain/model/collision compilation. Tile rotation matches RuneLite WorldPoint and the client terrain loader; object anchors reproduce the client footprint-aware Tiles.method2092/class69 formulas; cache-encoded generated/explicit heights replay loadTerrain semantics on the target plane; absent chunks reproduce the client's height seam filling; overlay rotation, tile flags, bridge behavior, object orientation, collision, model identity, GPU anchors and picker coordinates all follow the projected target scene. The legacy local RenderScene packet path remains unchanged while buildInstance explicitly rebases instance model geometry into the same world coordinate space as terrain.
entries.nextAction: Keep packed-template, all-four-rotation, raw height replay, missing-chunk seam, multi-tile object, bridge/collision and GPU world-space fixtures as regressions. Future instance editing UX or server-driven template acquisition should consume this projection contract rather than adding renderer-specific rotation.

entries.title: Wall orientation A/B bitfields
entries.nextAction: Retain the separate orientation contract in wall fixtures.

entries.title: Wall, corner, diagonal, and decoration model transforms
entries.reason: Wall and decoration variant decomposition now has one authoritative OSRS rule source. The fixture matrix covers wall shapes 0-3 and decoration shapes 4-8 across all four rotations, including L-wall dual variants, diagonal +4 rotations, opposite-facing decoration variants, and type-11 post-scale angle rotation. Packet-level fixtures cover the client isRotated XOR (rotation > 3) mirror rule, L-wall pair construction/normal merging, transform order, and real renderer-neutral placement.
entries.nextAction: Keep the full shape/rotation matrix and packet transform fixtures as regression coverage; track multi-tile scene bounds separately under objects.gameObjectFootprint.

entries.title: Wall neighbor normal merge and L-wall pair merge
entries.reason: L-wall pair normal merging, scene-wide shared-vertex normal accumulation, duplicate internal-face hiding, and cross-region wall joins are now covered. The live world-window renderer stitches adjacent 64x64 regions, materializes one padded multi-region document, and runs ModelPacketBuilder over that document; the boundary fixture proves merge-enabled walls on x=63/x=0 share normals and hide coincident seam faces across the region boundary.
entries.nextAction: Keep the L-wall and multi-region boundary fixtures as regression coverage when region materialization, model placement, or normal merging changes.

entries.title: Decorative object displacement and attached-wall relationship
entries.reason: Decoration shapes 4-8 are fixture-covered for all four rotations. Shapes 5, 6, and 8 inherit the supporting wall's decor displacement; straight placement uses the full displacement while diagonal placement uses the client half-displacement vector, with the fallback-16 rule retained when no wall exists. Shape 8 preserves distinct primary/secondary packets and the orientation-256 camera-dependent primary/secondary phase order used by Scene traversal.
entries.nextAction: Keep cardinal/diagonal displacement, fallback-16, shape-8 dual-renderable, and camera-order fixtures as regression coverage.

entries.title: Wall-decoration offsets, dual renderables, and wall-width compensation
entries.reason: Shape-8 wall decorations are preserved as distinct primary and secondary neutral model packets; primary carries the inherited wall-relative offset while secondary remains at the bare tile position, matching RuneLite's clickbox and Scene representation. Camera-side orientation-256 ordering is retained as renderer-neutral metadata and consumed by software/native ordering. Shapes 5/6/8 inherit supporting-wall displacement with the client's fallback of 16 when no wall is available.
entries.nextAction: Keep the shape-8 camera-order, supporting-wall displacement, fallback-16, and GPU-command propagation fixtures as regression coverage.

entries.title: Object footprint, orientation, and scene bounds
entries.reason: Game-object scene occupancy is now explicit and independent from renderable geometry bounds. Rotated definition footprints produce inclusive min/max occupied tiles and sizeX/sizeY; RuneLite-style object orientation is retained separately from model orientation, including shape 11's 256-JAU model orientation. Multilocs keep the placed definition's scene size even when a different fallback definition supplies the visible model. Metadata rebases with local-to-world scene projection, survives GPU command flattening and fingerprints, and is returned by picking alongside the exact ray-hit tile and object anchor.
entries.nextAction: Keep rotation, scene-edge, multiloc, world-rebase, GPU propagation, and picker fixtures as regressions; orientation-aware model AABB/radius remains tracked separately under models.bounds and native.picking.

entries.title: Ground objects and ground decorations
entries.nextAction: Add a cache-backed ground-decoration fixture.

entries.title: Face colors, unlit colors, and flat-face sentinels
entries.reason: Source/unlit Jagex HSL and post-lighting Model.faceColors1/2/3 are now explicit, independently asserted contracts. Recolor is applied before the retained unlit color, smooth and textured faces reproduce ModelData.toModel lighting/clamping, flat faces preserve faceColors3=-1 with the client's zero-initialized faceColors2 slot, and skipped faces preserve faceColors3=-2. Submission and GPU flattening use those sentinels directly, so textured renderType 3 is omitted correctly while 254-alpha shaded faces remain drawable. Flat color is expanded to three ordinary GPU vertex values only at the backend boundary. Optional unlit draw-mode negotiation remains tracked separately under callbacks.modes rather than being a color-retention gap.
entries.nextAction: Keep ModelFaceColorContract as the single source of truth when adding callback/unlit rendering modes or new dynamic model submission paths.

entries.title: Face alpha, hidden faces, and transparent render types
entries.nextAction: Include texture alpha in the same classification contract.

entries.title: Texture transparency in face-pass classification
entries.reason: Model texture cutouts remain in the opaque/depth-writing pass, blended model-face alpha remains in the sorted alpha pass, the native shader now matches RuneLite's base-LOD rule by discarding any model texture texel below fully opaque alpha, and UV animation direction/speed is covered by RuneLite-referenced fixtures.
entries.nextAction: Keep the RuneLite GPU alpha cutoff and animation-vector fixtures as regression coverage when texture filtering or animation timing changes.

entries.title: Renderable mode and depth participation
entries.nextAction: Add a native acceptance case for sorted/no-depth submission.

entries.title: Smooth versus flat normal construction

entries.title: Contour ground and height-map model placement
entries.reason: Static location contouring is now an explicit renderer/runtime contract. Raw contour type and parameter preserve cache/client clipType semantics; full, partial, extended and configured-but-skipped states are distinguishable; placement height and applied state are retained; warped packets preserve a 1:1 pre-contour Y stream that reconstructs RuneLite's HILLSKEW unskewed-model relationship; contour metadata propagates through GPU commands, fingerprints and PickResult. The builder preserves client ordering (animation/model transforms, pre-contour lighting, contour warp, then client bounds) and applies Scene wall-decoration displacement only after contour sampling.
entries.nextAction: Keep clipType mapping/overflow, full/partial/skipped contour, unskewed reconstruction, sloped placement, client-bounds recalculation, wall-decoration displacement ordering, GPU fingerprint and picker metadata fixtures as regressions. DrawCallbacks HILLSKEW negotiation remains tracked separately by callbacks.modes.

entries.title: Model bounds, radius, diameter, and bottom height
entries.reason: Client model bounds are now a first-class model-local contract: height, bottomY, xzRadius, radius, diameter, single-tile padding semantics, and orientation-specific AABB midpoint/half-extents reproduce the vendored client formulas. Bounds are calculated after model transforms and contouring but before scene footprint/decor placement translation, use the same draw orientation as client Scene traversal, remain unchanged by local-to-world anchor rebasing, retain one entry per client renderable for flattened multi-renderable shapes such as type-2 walls and compatibility shape-8 packets, propagate through GPU draw commands/fingerprints, and are exposed on PickResult without changing ray-selection behavior.
entries.nextAction: Keep cylinder/AABB, transform, contour, placement-separation, multi-renderable, rebase, GPU propagation, and picker-metadata fixtures as regressions. Native picking/culling behavior remains tracked separately.

entries.title: Texture definitions, pixels, and average-color fallback
evidence: GitHub Actions Revision 240 Texture Acceptance run 35718110830
entries.reason: Real revision-240 texture parity is now verified against OpenRS2 archive 2710 (oldschool/live/en build 240) using an independent RuneLite-melxin TextureLoader/SpriteManager exporter. The reference fixture selected texture 0 (opaque), 7 (RGB-zero cutout), and 17 (animated), each at 128x128 and brightness 0.6. The focused OsrsTextureRevisionVerifier detected revision 240, compared all 3 definitions/pixel rasters, and reported 0 differences with texture.parity PASS. The workflow artifact retains the generated metadata and SHA-256 pixel evidence without checking cache assets into the repository.
entries.nextAction: Keep the revision-240 acceptance workflow manual and rerun it when the supported revision, texture record decoder, sprite decode path, or texture pixel semantics change.

entries.title: Texture animation direction, speed, and offsets
entries.reason: Texture animation direction, speed, cache metadata transport, cycle phase, source-size scaling, native uniform state, and frame output are covered. RuneLite GPU supplies signed speed vectors and applies (gameCycle & 127) * speed / 128 in shader space; the software client performs the equivalent wrapped pixel shift. RSPSi centralizes the same phase math, preserves 64px and 128px texel speed, and the Xvfb/Mesa production-OpenGL acceptance proves animated output advances, a following static command cannot inherit the previous UV offset, and cycle 128 pixel-matches cycle 0.
entries.nextAction: Keep the shared TextureAnimation phase contract as the single source of truth and retain the native frame fixture when texture-array, sampling, or material batching changes.

entries.title: Valid fixed-axis occluder planes
entries.nextAction: Add camera-facing occlusion fixtures after wall joins are corrected.

entries.title: Scene visibility and effective-plane filtering
entries.reason: Client traversal now consumes the scene-wide minimum level and the per-tile physical/cull level as separate gates instead of equating visibility with authored or current-plane equality. The vanilla render profile uses CLIENT_TRAVERSAL; explicit authored/effective projections remain diagnostics. Current scene plane and cull level survive RenderConfig filtering, flow into GPU draw commands and fingerprints, prevent invalid terrain-range merging, and drive plane-correct occluder acceptance. Bridge-linked wall occluders are emitted on the shifted current scene plane, with fixtures covering visibility-below and bridge-shifted occlusion.
entries.nextAction: Retain the traversal, bridge, command-metadata, and occlusion fixtures as regressions while roof-region removal modes and future occluder sources are added.

entries.title: OpenGL framebuffer, depth, blend, cull, and polygon state
entries.nextAction: Keep first-GL-error and framebuffer diagnostics in native acceptance output.

entries.title: Opaque/alpha draw ranges, batching, and diagnostics
entries.reason: Opaque/alpha separation and native draw-call grouping are now expressed by a backend-neutral planner. Synthetic fixtures verify material, depth-mode, priority-order, submission-pass, and 8x8 resident-zone boundaries without requiring a live GL context.
entries.nextAction: Keep the synthetic batching fixtures aligned with future render-state keys so incompatible draw ranges cannot silently merge.

entries.title: Depth modes, face bias, priority ordering, and winding/facing
entries.reason: Depth mode, scene/model category priority, face priority, face bias, and model-facing behavior are now covered. BackfacePolicy owns the RuneLite-derived facing contract; client-visible Model.draw0 faces map to GL_CCW after the Y-down client viewport to Y-up OpenGL conversion. Native model rendering defaults to Client Front, terrain remains deliberately two-sided, mirror/rotation variants preserve winding, and the Xvfb/Mesa pixel acceptance exercises the production OpenGL 3.3 path: Client Front renders the accepted face, Reversed Debug rejects it, Two Sided matches Client Front for that face, and terrain is unchanged by either diagnostic winding.
entries.nextAction: Keep client-front GL_CCW as the default model policy and keep terrain two-sided until shaped-tile winding is addressed as a separate lower-priority parity item.

entries.title: Scene object and tile picking
entries.reason: Object and tile picking now carries deterministic per-scene object-instance identity derived from authored placement plus a duplicate-occurrence ordinal, preserving identity across packet/GPU/incremental rebuild boundaries and distinguishing same-definition placements and exact duplicate cache entries. Client-local orientation-aware Model AABBs are used as a conservative broad phase before exact world-triangle intersection; per-renderable scene-placement offsets preserve displaced wall-decoration and multi-renderable transforms, and legacy local RenderScene geometry keeps a separate render-space anchor from its world semantic identity. Exact triangle hits, occlusion, plane restriction, priority tie-breaking, game-object footprint metadata, and client model bounds remain the authoritative final pick contract.
entries.nextAction: Keep stable-instance, duplicate-placement, local/world rebase, multi-renderable, displaced-decoration, AABB rejection, overlapping-AABB exact-hit, terrain-merge, and incremental-rebuild fixtures as regressions. A future native ID framebuffer may optimize the backend without changing PickResult semantics.

entries.title: Actors, NPCs, players, and animated models
entries.reason: Static map editing is the current gate; dynamic actor submission is inventory-only.
entries.nextAction: Audit animation height offsets, scene identity, and dynamic material submission in a later phase.

entries.title: Sequence frames, animation height offset, and frame-time transforms
entries.reason: Covered by raw sequence/skeleton/cached-animation decoding plus legacy and cached frame selection, signed animation-height offsets, stable scene identity, animation-before-contour ordering, frame-time scene refresh, cached curve/bone/alpha application, and incremental GPU rebuild acceptance.
entries.nextAction: Keep these fixtures as regressions. Actor dual-animation blending, NPC/player animation systems, instances, and unrelated runtime animation work remain separately scoped.

entries.title: Dynamic material and texture-array submission
entries.reason: Dynamic material changes are outside the static map acceptance gate.
entries.nextAction: Audit material lifetime and animated texture binding with dynamic entity fixtures.

entries.title: Projectiles and graphics/spot animations
entries.reason: These are not part of the static map-editor renderer gate.
entries.nextAction: Create dynamic render-mode and animation fixtures after static parity.

entries.title: Ground items and item-layer rendering
entries.reason: Inventory is documented for review but item entities are outside the static map gate.
entries.nextAction: Add item-layer identity, stacking, and picking fixtures in the dynamic phase.

entries.title: RuneLite draw callback modes and optional passes
entries.reason: The native renderer now has an explicit fail-closed DrawCallbacks compatibility contract using the vendored RuneLite bit/pass values. GPU, HILLSKEW, NORMALS and ZBUF are advertised because each has concrete backing state; unsupported optional flags remain disabled instead of being silently claimed. The only pass IDs in the vendored API are PASS_OPAQUE and PASS_ALPHA, and both map directly to GpuDrawCommand submission passes. HILLSKEW uses retained pre-contour model state, normals survive into GPU-plan vertices, all five render modes have explicit native depth/blend state, and production OpenGL acceptance verifies alpha composition occurs after opaque submission with depth state restored afterward.
entries.nextAction: Keep callback negotiation, contour/normal transport, render-mode state and native opaque/alpha composition fixtures as regressions. Add future RuneLite callback capabilities only when a source-backed editor feature requires and implements them.
